knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 2.5.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly states the central limit theorem for a sample mean?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the CLT conditions and target.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: The theorem concerns the distribution of the standardised sum or mean, not individual observations, under stated conditions.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: For iid finite-variance data, X̄≈N(μ,σ²/n) for large n.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Applying the CLT to one observation or forgetting the √n reduction in standard deviation.

choices.label: For iid observations with finite mean μ and variance σ², the standardised sample mean approaches N(0,1), so X̄ is approximately N(μ,σ²/n) for large n.
The CLT makes each individual observation approximately Normal as n grows.
The CLT applies only when the parent population is already Normal.
The sample mean has variance σ² rather than σ²/n because averaging changes only its mean.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: CLT probability for sample mean
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Pet-insurance claim severities are iid with mean μ = 180 and standard deviation σ = 60. A sample of n = 36 claims is drawn. Using the CLT and Φ(1) ≈ 0.841, approximate P(X̄ < 170). Enter the probability as a decimal.
knowledge_checks.body: Standardise the sample mean under the CLT and evaluate the lower tail.
hints: First form sd(X̄) = σ/√n, then z = (170 - 180)/sd(X̄).
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Using σ = 60 instead of σ/√n = 10 so that z = -1/6, or reporting Φ(1) ≈ 0.841 as the lower-tail probability itself.
success_criteria: Uses σ/√n when standardising, and converts Φ(1) to the lower tail.

worked_example.title: CLT probability for a mean pet-insurance severity
worked_example.problem_statement: Pet-insurance claim severities are iid with mean μ = 180 and standard deviation σ = 60. A sample of n = 36 claims is drawn. Using the CLT, approximate P(X̄ < 170). Use Φ(1) ≈ 0.841.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Form the sampling sd σ/√n first, then standardise 170 before reading Φ.

steps.label: Standard error of the sample mean
steps.explanation: Under the CLT for iid observations, X̄ is approximately Normal with mean μ and sd σ/√n.

steps.label: Standardise and evaluate the lower tail
steps.attempt_cue: Form z = (170 − 180)/10, then convert with Φ.
steps.explanation: The probability is the lower Normal tail at z = −1, equal to 1 − Φ(1).

steps.label: Refuse σ in place of σ/√n
steps.attempt_cue: State why using sd = 60 for X̄ is wrong.
steps.explanation: The CLT approximates the distribution of the sample mean, whose spread shrinks by √n. Using the population sd as if it were sd(X̄) ignores that reduction.

worked_example.final_answer: X̄ ≈ Normal(180, 10); z = −1; P(X̄ < 170) ≈ 0.159. Casual Normal use without stating the IID CLT sampling sd is not the same skill.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Using X̄ ≈ Normal(180, 60) and computing z = (170 − 180)/60 = −1/6, or reading Φ(1) ≈ 0.841 as the lower-tail probability itself.
